{{short description|On  the approximate structure of sets whose sumset is small}}
In [[additive combinatorics]], a discipline within mathematics, '''Freiman's theorem''' is a central result which indicates the approximate structure of sets whose [[sumset]] is small. It roughly states that if <math>|A+A|/|A|</math> is small, then <math>A</math> can be contained in a small [[generalized arithmetic progression]].

==Statement==
If <math>A</math> is a finite subset of <math>\mathbb{Z}</math> with <math>|A+A|\le K|A|</math>, then <math>A</math> is contained in a generalized arithmetic progression of dimension at most <math>d(K)</math> and size at most <math>f(K)|A|</math>, where <math>d(K)</math> and <math>f(K)</math> are constants depending only on <math>K</math>.

==Examples==
For a finite set <math>A</math> of integers, it is always true that

:<math>|A + A| \ge 2|A|-1,</math>

with equality precisely when <math>A</math> is an arithmetic progression.

More generally, suppose <math>A</math> is a subset of a finite proper generalized arithmetic progression <math>P</math> of dimension <math>d</math> such that <math>|P| \le C|A|</math> for some real <math>C \ge 1</math>. Then <math>|P+P| \le 2^d |P|</math>, so that

:<math>|A+A| \le |P+P| \le 2^d |P| \le C2^d|A|.</math>

==History of Freiman's theorem==
This result is due to [[Gregory Freiman]] (1964, 1966).<ref>{{cite journal | zbl=0163.29501 | last=Freiman | first=G.A. | author-link=Gregory Freiman | title=Addition of finite sets | language=en | journal=Soviet Mathematics. Doklady | volume=5 | pages=1366–1370 | year=1964 }}</ref><ref>{{cite book | first=G. A. | last=Freiman | author-link=Gregory Freiman | title=Foundations of a Structural Theory of Set Addition | language=ru | publisher=Kazan Gos. Ped. Inst. | location=Kazan | year=1966 | page=140 | zbl=0203.35305  }}</ref><ref>{{cite book| last=Nathanson | first=Melvyn B. | year=1996 | title=Additive Number Theory: Inverse Problems and Geometry of Sumsets | volume=165 | series=[[Graduate Texts in Mathematics]] | publisher=Springer | isbn=978-0-387-94655-9 | zbl=0859.11003}} p. 252.</ref>  Much interest in it, and applications, stemmed from a new proof by [[Imre Z. Ruzsa]] (1992,1994).<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Ruzsa |first=I. Z. |date=August 1992 |title=Arithmetical progressions and the number of sums |url=http://link.springer.com/10.1007/BF02454387 |journal=Periodica Mathematica Hungarica |language=en |volume=25 |issue=1 |pages=105–111 |doi=10.1007/BF02454387 |issn=0031-5303|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | first=Imre Z. | last=Ruzsa | author-link=Imre Z. Ruzsa | title=Generalized arithmetical progressions and sumsets | journal=[[Acta Mathematica Hungarica]] | volume=65 | number=4  | year=1994 | pages=379–388 | zbl=0816.11008 | doi=10.1007/bf01876039 | doi-access=free}}</ref>  [[Mei-Chu Chang]] proved new polynomial estimates for the size of arithmetic progressions arising in the theorem in 2002.<ref>{{cite journal|date=2002|title=A polynomial bound in Freiman's theorem|journal=Duke Mathematical Journal|volume=113|pages=399–419|mr=1909605|last1=Chang|first1=Mei-Chu|number=3|doi=10.1215/s0012-7094-02-11331-3}}</ref> The current best bounds were provided by [[Tom Sanders (mathematician)|Tom Sanders]].<ref>{{cite journal|first=Tom|last=Sanders|author-link=Tom Sanders (mathematician)|date=2013|title=The structure theory of set addition revisited|journal=Bulletin of the American Mathematical Society|volume=50|pages=93–127|doi=10.1090/S0273-0979-2012-01392-7 |arxiv=1212.0458|s2cid=42609470 }}</ref>

==Tools used in the proof==
The proof presented here follows the proof in Yufei Zhao's lecture notes.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Zhao |first1=Yufei |title=Graph Theory and Additive Combinatorics |url=http://yufeizhao.com/gtac/fa17/gtac.pdf |access-date=2019-12-02 |archive-date=2019-11-23 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191123230241/http://yufeizhao.com/gtac/fa17/gtac.pdf }}</ref>

===Plünnecke–Ruzsa inequality===
{{Main|Plünnecke–Ruzsa inequality}}

===Ruzsa covering lemma===
The Ruzsa covering lemma states the following:

:Let <math>A</math> and <math>S</math> be finite subsets of an [[abelian group]] with <math>S</math> nonempty, and let <math>K</math> be a positive real number. Then if <math>|A+S| \le K|S|</math>, there is a subset <math>T</math> of <math>A</math> with at most <math>K</math> elements such that <math>A \subseteq T+S-S</math>.

This lemma provides a bound on how many copies of <math>S-S</math> one needs to cover <math>A</math>, hence the name. The proof is essentially a [[greedy algorithm]]:

'''Proof:''' Let <math>T</math> be a maximal subset of <math>A</math> such that the sets <math>t+S</math> for <math>A</math> are all disjoint. Then <math>|T+S|=|T| \cdot |S|</math>, and also <math>|T+S| \le |A+S| \le K|S|</math>, so <math>|T| \le K</math>. Furthermore, for any <math>a \in A</math>, there is some <math>t \in T</math> such that <math>t+S</math> intersects <math>a+S</math>, as otherwise adding <math>a</math> to <math>T</math> contradicts the maximality of <math>T</math>. Thus <math>a \in T+S-S</math>, so <math>A \subseteq T+S-S</math>.

===Freiman homomorphisms and the Ruzsa modeling lemma===
Let <math>s \ge 2</math> be a positive integer, and <math>\Gamma</math> and <math>\Gamma'</math> be abelian groups. Let <math>A \subseteq \Gamma</math> and <math>B \subseteq \Gamma'</math>. A map <math>\varphi \colon A \to B</math> is a '''Freiman <math>s</math>-homomorphism''' if
:<math>\varphi(a_1) + \cdots + \varphi(a_s) = \varphi(a_1') + \cdots + \varphi(a_s')</math>
whenever <math>a_1 + \cdots + a_s = a_1' + \cdots + a_s'</math> for any <math>a_1, \ldots, a_s, a_1', \ldots, a_s' \in A</math>.

If in addition <math>\varphi</math> is a bijection and <math>\varphi^{-1} \colon B \to A</math> is a Freiman <math>s</math>-homomorphism, then <math>\varphi</math> is a Freiman '''<math>s</math>-isomorphism'''.

If <math>\varphi</math> is a Freiman <math>s</math>-homomorphism, then <math>\varphi</math> is a Freiman <math>t</math>-homomorphism for any positive integer <math>t</math> such that <math>2\le t \le s</math>.

Then the Ruzsa modeling lemma states the following:

:Let <math>A</math> be a finite set of integers, and let <math>s \ge 2</math> be a positive integer. Let <math>N</math> be a positive integer such that <math>N \ge |sA-sA|</math>. Then there exists a subset <math>A'</math> of <math>A</math> with cardinality at least <math>|A|/s</math> such that <math>A'</math> is Freiman <math>s</math>-isomorphic to a subset of <math>\mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z}</math>.

The last statement means there exists some Freiman <math>s</math>-homomorphism between the two subsets.

'''Proof sketch:''' Choose a prime <math>q</math> sufficiently large such that the modulo-<math>q</math> reduction map <math>\pi_q \colon \mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{Z}/q\mathbb{Z}</math> is a Freiman <math>s</math>-isomorphism from <math>A</math> to its image in <math>\mathbb{Z}/q\mathbb{Z}</math>. Let <math>\psi_q \colon \mathbb{Z}/q\mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{Z}</math> be the lifting map that takes each member of <math>\mathbb{Z}/q\mathbb{Z}</math> to its unique representative in <math>\{1,\ldots,q\} \subseteq \mathbb{Z}</math>. For nonzero <math>\lambda \in \mathbb{Z}/q\mathbb{Z}</math>, let <math>\cdot\lambda \colon \mathbb{Z}/q\mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{Z}/q\mathbb{Z}</math> be the multiplication by <math>\lambda</math> map, which is a Freiman <math>s</math>-isomorphism. Let <math>B</math> be the image <math>(\cdot\lambda\circ\pi_q)(A)</math>. Choose a suitable subset <math>B'</math> of <math>B</math> with cardinality at least <math>|B|/s</math> such that the restriction of <math>\psi_q</math> to <math>B'</math> is a Freiman <math>s</math>-isomorphism onto its image, and let <math>A' \subseteq A</math> be the preimage of <math>B'</math> under <math>\cdot\lambda\circ\pi_q</math>. Then the restriction of <math>\psi_q \circ \cdot\lambda \circ \pi_q</math> to <math>A'</math> is a Freiman <math>s</math>-isomorphism onto its image <math>\psi_q(B')</math>. Lastly, there exists some choice of nonzero <math>\lambda</math> such that the restriction of the modulo-<math>N</math> reduction <math>\mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z}</math> to <math>\psi_q(B')</math> is a Freiman <math>s</math>-isomorphism onto its image. The result follows after composing this map with the earlier Freiman <math>s</math>-isomorphism.

===Bohr sets and Bogolyubov's lemma===
Though Freiman's theorem applies to sets of integers, the Ruzsa modeling lemma allows one to model sets of integers as subsets of finite [[cyclic group]]s. So it is useful to first work in the setting of a [[finite field]], and then generalize results to the integers. The following lemma was proved by Bogolyubov:

:Let <math>A \subseteq \mathbb{F}_2^n</math> and let <math>\alpha= |A|/2^n</math>. Then <math>4A</math> contains a subspace of <math>\mathbb{F}_2^n</math> of dimension at least <math>n-\alpha^{-2}</math>.

Generalizing this lemma to arbitrary cyclic groups requires an analogous notion to "subspace": that of the Bohr set. Let <math>R</math> be a subset of <math>\mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z}</math> where <math>N</math> is a prime. The '''Bohr set''' of dimension <math>|R|</math> and width <math>\varepsilon</math> is 

:<math>\operatorname{Bohr}(R, \varepsilon) = \{ x \in \mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z} : \forall r \in R, |rx/N| \le \varepsilon \},</math>

where <math>|rx/N|</math> is the distance from <math>rx/N</math> to the nearest integer. The following lemma generalizes Bogolyubov's lemma:

:Let <math>A \subseteq \mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z}</math> and <math>\alpha = |A|/N</math>. Then <math>2A-2A</math> contains a Bohr set of dimension at most <math>\alpha^{-2}</math> and width <math>1/4</math>.

Here the dimension of a Bohr set is analogous to the [[codimension]] of a set in <math>\mathbb{F}_2^n</math>. The proof of the lemma involves [[Fourier analysis|Fourier-analytic]] methods. The following proposition relates Bohr sets back to generalized arithmetic progressions, eventually leading to the proof of Freiman's theorem.

:Let <math>X</math> be a Bohr set in <math>\mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z}</math> of dimension <math>d</math> and width <math>\varepsilon</math>. Then <math>X</math> contains a proper generalized arithmetic progression of dimension at most <math>d</math> and size at least <math>(\varepsilon/d)^dN</math>.

The proof of this proposition uses [[Minkowski's theorem]], a fundamental result in [[geometry of numbers]].

==Proof==
By the Plünnecke–Ruzsa inequality, <math>|8A-8A|\le K^{16}|A|</math>. By [[Bertrand's postulate]], there exists a prime <math>N</math> such that <math>|8A-8A|\le N\le 2K^{16}|A|</math>. By the Ruzsa modeling lemma, there exists a subset <math>A'</math> of <math>A</math> of cardinality at least <math>|A|/8</math> such that <math>A'</math> is Freiman 8-isomorphic to a subset <math>B\subseteq \mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z}</math>.

By the generalization of Bogolyubov's lemma, <math>2B-2B</math> contains a proper generalized arithmetic progression of dimension <math>d</math> at most <math>(1/(8\cdot 2K^{16}))^{-2}=256K^{32}</math> and size at least <math>(1/(4d))^dN</math>. Because <math>A'</math> and <math>B</math> are Freiman 8-isomorphic, <math>2A'-2A'</math> and <math>2B-2B</math> are Freiman 2-isomorphic. Then the image under the 2-isomorphism of the proper generalized arithmetic progression in <math>2B-2B</math> is a proper generalized arithmetic progression in <math>2A'-2A'\subseteq 2A-2A</math> called <math>P</math>.

But <math>P+A\subseteq 3A-2A</math>, since <math>P\subseteq 2A-2A</math>. Thus 
:<math>|P+A|\le |3A-2A|\le |8A-8A|\le N\le (4d)^d|P|</math>
so by the Ruzsa covering lemma <math>A\subseteq X+P-P</math> for some <math>X\subseteq A</math> of cardinality at most <math>(4d)^d</math>. Then <math>X+P-P</math> is contained in a generalized arithmetic progression of dimension <math>|X|+d</math> and size at most <math>2^{|X|}2^{d}|P|\le 2^{|X|+d}|2A-2A|\le 2^{|X|+d}K^4|A|</math>, completing the proof.

==Generalizations==
{{See also|Arithmetic combinatorics#Breuillard–Green–Tao_theorem}}

A result due to [[Ben Green (mathematician)|Ben Green]] and Imre Ruzsa generalized Freiman's theorem to arbitrary abelian groups. They used an analogous notion to generalized arithmetic progressions, which they called coset progressions. A '''coset progression''' of an abelian group <math>G</math> is a set <math>P+H</math> for a proper generalized arithmetic progression <math>P</math> and a subgroup <math>H</math> of <math>G</math>. The dimension of this coset progression is defined to be the dimension of <math>P</math>, and its size is defined to be the cardinality of the whole set. Green and Ruzsa showed the following:

:Let <math>A</math> be a finite set in an abelian group <math>G</math> such that <math>|A+A| \le K|A|</math>. Then <math>A</math> is contained in a coset progression of dimension at most <math>d(K)</math> and size at most <math>f(K)|A|</math>, where <math>f(K)</math> and <math>d(K)</math> are functions of <math>K</math> that are independent of <math>G</math>.

Green and Ruzsa provided upper bounds of <math>d(K)=CK^4\log (K+2)</math> and <math>f(K)=e^{CK^4\log^2(K+2)}</math> for some absolute constant <math>C</math>.<ref> {{cite journal | first1=Imre Z. | last1=Ruzsa | author-link=Imre Z. Ruzsa |last2 =Green | first2 = Ben | author-link2 = Ben Green (mathematician) | title=Freiman's theorem in an arbitrary abelian group | journal=  Journal of the London Mathematical Society| volume=75 | number=1  | year=2007 | pages=163–175 | doi=10.1112/jlms/jdl021| arxiv=math/0505198 | s2cid=15115236 }} </ref>

[[Terence Tao]] (2010) also generalized Freiman's theorem to [[solvable group]]s of bounded derived length.<ref> {{cite journal | first=Terence | last=Tao| author-link=Terence Tao | title=Freiman's theorem for solvable groups | journal = Contributions to Discrete Mathematics | volume=5 | number=2 | year=2010 | pages=137–184 | doi=10.11575/cdm.v5i2.62020 | doi-access=free}} </ref>

Extending Freiman's theorem to an arbitrary nonabelian group is still open. Results for <math>K<2</math>, when a set has very small doubling, are referred to as [[Kneser%27s theorem (combinatorics) | Kneser]] theorems.<ref> {{cite web |last1=Tao |first1=Terence |author-link = Terence Tao|title=An elementary non-commutative Freiman theorem | url=https://terrytao.wordpress.com/2009/11/10/an-elementary-non-commutative-freiman-theorem/ |website=Terence Tao's blog|date=10 November 2009 }} </ref>

The polynomial Freiman–Ruzsa conjecture<ref>{{Cite web |date=2007-03-11 |title=(Ben Green) The Polynomial Freiman–Ruzsa conjecture |url=https://terrytao.wordpress.com/2007/03/11/ben-green-the-polynomial-freiman-ruzsa-conjecture/ |access-date=2023-11-14 |website=What's new |language=en}}</ref> is a generalization published in a paper<ref>{{cite journal |last=Ruzsa |first=I. |year=1999 |title=An analog of Freiman's theorem in groups |url=http://www.numdam.org/article/AST_1999__258__323_0.pdf |journal=Astérisque |volume=258 |pages=323–326}}</ref> by [[Imre Z. Ruzsa|Imre Ruzsa]] but credited by him to [[Katalin Marton]]. It states that if a subset of a group (a power of a [[cyclic group]]) <math>A\subset G</math> has [[Additive combinatorics#Doubling constant|doubling constant]] such that <math>|A+A|\le K|A|</math>, then it is covered by a bounded number <math>K^{C}</math>of cosets of some subgroup <math>H\subset G</math> with<math>|H|\le |A|</math>. In 2012, [[Tom Sanders (mathematician)|Tom Sanders]] gave an almost-polynomial bound of the conjecture for abelian groups.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Sanders |first=Tom |date=2012-10-15 |title=On the Bogolyubov–Ruzsa lemma |url=http://msp.org/apde/2012/5-3/p05.xhtml |journal=Analysis & PDE |language=en |volume=5 |issue=3 |pages=627–655 |doi=10.2140/apde.2012.5.627 |issn=1948-206X|doi-access=free |arxiv=1011.0107 }}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Brubaker |first=Ben |date=2023-12-04 |title=An Easy-Sounding Problem Yields Numbers Too Big for Our Universe |url=https://www.quantamagazine.org/an-easy-sounding-problem-yields-numbers-too-big-for-our-universe-20231204/ |access-date=2023-12-11 |website=Quanta Magazine |language=en}}</ref> In 2023, a solution over <math>G=\mathbb F_2^n</math> a field of characteristic 2 has been posted as a preprint by [[Timothy Gowers|Tim Gowers]], [[Ben Green (mathematician)|Ben Green]], Freddie Manners, and [[Terence Tao|Terry Tao]].<ref>{{Cite arXiv |last1=Gowers |first1=W. T. |last2=Green |first2=Ben |last3=Manners |first3=Freddie |last4=Tao |first4=Terence |date=2023 |title=On a conjecture of Marton |class=math.NT |eprint=2311.05762}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-11-13 |title=On a conjecture of Marton |url=https://terrytao.wordpress.com/2023/11/13/on-a-conjecture-of-marton/ |access-date=2023-11-14 |website=What's new |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Sloman |first=Leila |date=December 6, 2023 |title='A-Team' of Math Proves a Critical Link Between Addition and Sets |url=https://www.quantamagazine.org/a-team-of-math-proves-a-critical-link-between-addition-and-sets-20231206/?mc_cid=cda01dcc5c |access-date=December 16, 2023 |website=Quanta Magazine}}</ref> This proof was completely formalized in the [[Lean (proof assistant)|Lean 4]] formal proof language, a collaborative project that marked an important milestone in terms of mathematicians successfully formalizing contemporary mathematics.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://teorth.github.io/pfr/ |website=PFR Project homepage| language=en |title=The Polynomial Freiman-Ruzsa Conjecture }}</ref>
